ITQAN:v2p315/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p315/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p315/r4.claim: فاستعصم means he refrained or held himself back.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya glosses istaʿṣama as seeking and holding fast to protection, and resisting her.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r5.anchor: فاستعصم قال ابن عطية: معناه طلب العصمة، وتمسك بها وعصاني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes istaʿṣama as an intensive pattern expressing powerful refusal and guardedness, as if Joseph were already protected but strove for more.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: والاستعصام بناء مبالغة يدل على الامتناع البليغ والتحفظ الشديد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats Joseph's refusal as a clear proof against interpretations that attribute sinful desire to him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r7.anchor: وهذا بيان لما كان من يوسف عليه السلام لا مزيد عليه، وبرهان لا شيء أنور منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers the grammarians' analysis: istaʿṣama matches iʿtaṣama and denotes actual protection, not seeking it or a special intensification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r8.anchor: والذي ذكر التصريفيون في استعصم أنه موافق لاعتصم، فاستفعل فيه موافق لافتعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r9.claim: The analogies cited for intensification also match the iftiʿāl pattern; istafḥala instead matches tafaʿʿala.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272/r9.anchor: وأما استمسك واستوسع واستجمع الرأي فاستفعل فيه موافقة لافتعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r1.claim: The first object of آمر is omitted, with the sense that she commands Joseph to do something; if ما is a verbal noun, its pronoun instead returns to Joseph.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r1.anchor: ومفعول آمر الأول محذوف، وكان التقدير ما آمره به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r2.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r2.claim: One group reads وليكونن with a doubled nūn; the written alif reflects the majority's light nūn reading and remains in pausal spelling, as in al-Aʿshā's verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r2.anchor: وقرأت فرقة: وليكونن بالنون المشددة، وكتبها في المصحف بالألف مراعاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r4.claim: She threatened painful punishment in the earlier scene while still angry and denying her pursuit; now she is hopeful, has justified herself to the women, and threatens prison instead.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r4.anchor: ولم يذكر هنا العذاب الأليم الذي ذكرته في ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r5.claim: The women urge Joseph to obey, framing compliance as preferable to imprisonment and humiliation; his answer attributes the call to them because they counsel and adorn compliance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p272#2/r5.anchor: وقال له النسوة: أطع وافعل ما أمرتك به، فقال: رب السجن أحب إلي

MAJAZ:v1p310/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p310/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p310/r6.claim: Rabbika in Joseph's request means your human master or owner.
MAJAZ:v1p310/r6.anchor: «اذكرني عند ربك» (32) أي عند سيدك من بنى آدم ومولاك وقال:

MAJAZ:v1p310/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p310/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p310/r7.claim: An anonymous poem uses rabb for the owner of a herd.
MAJAZ:v1p310/r7.anchor: فإن يك رب أذواد بحسمى ... أصابوا من لقائك ما أصابوا

MAJAZ:v1p310/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p310/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p310/r8.claim: Al-Aʿshā's poem names al-Nuʿmān as rabb; anshada means he gave when asked in written petitions.
MAJAZ:v1p310/r8.anchor:
[قال الأعشى:
ربى كريم لا يكدر نعمة ... وإذا تنوشد فى المهارق أنشدا
يعنى النعمان إذا سئل بالمهارق الكتب، أنشدا: أعطى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p34/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p34/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p34/r7.claim: The wife admits that she seduced Joseph and that he resisted, then threatens imprisonment if he disobeys; the threat is meant to shame and separate him from her.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p34/r7.anchor: { راودته عن نفسه } أي لأصل إليه بما أريد { فاستعصم }

BIQAI-FULL:v4p34/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p34/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p34/r8.claim: The heavy emphatic nūn strengthens the threat of imprisonment, while the lighter nūn marks the threat of humiliation; alternatively, prison receives stronger emphasis because it separates the beloved.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p34/r8.anchor: أكدتهع بالنون الثقيلة وقالت : { وليكونا } بالنون الخفيفة

DURR-FULL:v4p503/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r4.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r4.claim: The wife admits she tried to seduce Joseph and says he resisted after he had loosened his trousers, though she does not know what changed his mind.
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r4.anchor: بعدما كان حل سراويله ثم لا أدري ما بدا له

DURR-FULL:v4p532/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p532/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p532/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses Joseph's steadfastness as refusal; Qatadah says he resisted.
DURR-FULL:v4p532/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {فاستعصم} قال: امتنع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p241/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p241/r1.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p241/r1.claim: Al-Tabari takes the woman's words to mean: 'This is the man over whom you blamed me,' the one whose sake made her err in passion; the pronoun in فيه refers to Joseph. Alternatively, the gesture is to her love of Joseph and the pronoun refers to that love.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p241/r1.anchor: قال الطبري: المعنى: فهذا الذي لمتنني فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p241/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p241/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p241/r2.claim: The wife of al-Aziz admits to seducing Joseph and appeals to the women because she knows they excuse her; استعصم means he sought and held to protection, before she threatens him while he hears.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p241/r2.anchor: ثم أقرت امرأة العزيز للنسوة بالمراودة واستنامت إليهن في ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p241/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p241/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p241/r3.claim: In ليسجنن the first lām introduces an oath, the next is the oath lām, and the nūn is emphatic and doubled at pause; وليكونا has a light nūn and pauses with alif, like 96:15 and the line of al-A'sha. A group reads its nūn doubled; الصاغرين are the humiliated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p241/r3.anchor: لام القسم، واللام الأولى هي المؤذنة بمجيء القسم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r1.claim: The commentators say the women were overcome with desire and cut their hands when she identified Joseph as the man they had blamed her for loving.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r1.anchor: لما ذهبت عقولهن فقطعن أيديهن قالت لهن ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r2.claim: To explain how she points while Joseph is present, Ibn al-Anbari says she indicated him after he had left the gathering.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنها أشارت ب ذلكن إلى يوسف بعد انصرافه من المجلس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, an omitted “this is” yields “here is the one you blamed me for,” so she can speak while Joseph is present.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r3.anchor: والثاني أن في الكلام إضمار هذا تقديره فهذا ذلكن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r4.claim: “You blamed me for” means blaming her for loving him; she then admits she tried to seduce him, and he resisted.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r4.anchor: ومعنى لمتنني فيه أي في حبه ثم أقرت عندهن فقالت ( ولقد راودته عن نفسه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the light nūn in “he will surely be among the humiliated”; at pause the light nūn becomes an alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج القراءة الجيدة تخفيف وليكونن والوقوف عليها بالألف لأن النون الخفيفة تبدل منها في الوقف الألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj dislikes the doubled-nūn reading because it conflicts with the codex and the doubled nūn has no pause substitution; ṣāghirūn means humiliated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p219#2/r6.anchor: وقد قرئت وليكونن بتشديد النون وأكرهها لخلاف المصحف لأن الشديدة لا يبدل منها شيء والصاغرون المذلون

JISHUMI:v5p3637/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r1.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r1.claim: Yaʿqūb alone reads السجن with fatḥa on sīn as a verbal noun; the others use kasra for the prison as a place.
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r1.anchor: قرأ يعقوب وحده: (السجن) بفتح السين على المصدر

JISHUMI:v5p3637/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r2.claim: Lawm is reproach or blame; related forms describe the blameworthy person or thing, and blame resembles disparagement that describes something bad with contempt, opposite praise.
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r2.anchor: اللوم: العذل لمته ألومه لوما، ورجل ملوم، والمليم الذي يستحق اللوم

JISHUMI:v5p3637/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r3.claim: Sijn means preventing someone from acting by confinement; the jailer administers it, and sijn with kasra can name the prison.
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r3.anchor: والسجن: المنع عن التصرف بالحبس، سجن يسجن سجنا، والسجان: المتولي للحبس

JISHUMI:v5p3637/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r5.claim: Ṣaghār is humiliation; ṣabā means inclination or desire, and the cited line about Hind shows the word's sense of the heart inclining.
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r5.anchor: الصبو: الميل إلى الشيء، صبا صبوا وصبى وصبوا وصباء

JISHUMI:v5p3637/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r6.claim: The related hamzated ṣābiʾ and plural ṣubāʾ describe someone who leans from one religion to another.
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r6.anchor: ومنه: الصابئ بالهمز، وجمعه: صبا على وزن فعال من صبأ، أي: مال من دين إلى دين

JISHUMI:v5p3637/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r8.claim: The final nūn in ليكونا is emphatic and may be light or heavy; the nūn in ليسجنن is heavy, and pause forms differ from connected speech, as in لنسفعا.
JISHUMI:v5p3637/r8.anchor: النون في قوله: [(ليكونا)] نون التأكيد، وهي تخفف وتشدد

JISHUMI:v5p3641/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r3.claim: The passage establishes Joseph's innocence because he resisted and protected himself from the sin.
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r3.anchor: تدل الآية على براءة يوسف لذلك قال: فاستعصم

JISHUMI:v5p3641/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r6.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r6.claim: Al-Aṣamm says the women imposed the apparent punishment of imprisonment but did not succeed in corrupting Joseph's religion.
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r6.anchor: قال الأصم: تدل على أنهم أظهروا العقوبة في نفسه، ولم يصرن إلى شيء من فساد دينه

JISHUMI:v5p3641/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r7.claim: Their plotting and imprisonment were their own acts, not created by God.
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r7.anchor: وتدل على أن تلك الأفعال والكيد والسجن فعلهم، وليس بخلق لله تعالى

MUQATIL:12:31-33/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:31-33/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:31-33/r2.claim: Zulaykha told the women Joseph was the one they blamed her for desiring; he refused intercourse, so she threatened to imprison and disgrace him.
MUQATIL:12:31-33/r2.anchor: { قالت } زليخا: { فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه } الذي افتتنتن به، { ولقد راودته عن نفسه فاستعصم } ، يعني فامتنع عن الجماع،

ZAJJAJ:v3p108/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p108/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p108/r1.claim: The good reading has light nūn in layakūnā; at pause the light nūn becomes alif, as in the imperative example. He rejects the heavy-nūn reading as contrary to the codex.
ZAJJAJ:v3p108/r1.anchor: القراءة الجيدة تخفيف ليكونا. والوقوف عليها بالألف

ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

TABATABAI:12:32-33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:32-33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:32-33/r1.claim: The women's infatuation erased their restraint; the Aziz's wife openly admitted her seduction attempt and threatened Yusuf with prison and humiliation if he disobeyed.
TABATABAI:12:32-33/r1.anchor: فأبدت سرا ما كانت تعترف به قبل ثم هددت يوسف تجلدا وحفظا لمقامها

TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r1.claim: The narration omits an intervening question about what the wife said; she points to Joseph as the very man for whom they blamed her, making direct sight the strongest reply.
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r1.anchor: الكلام في موضع دفن الدخل كأن قائلا يقول فماذا قالت امرأة العزيز

TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r2.claim: Pointing listeners to what they can see is the strongest form of explanation, as in the cited examples from al-Anbiyaʾ and al-Aʿraf.
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r2.anchor: وأقوى البيان أن يحال السامع إلى العيان

TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r3.claim: She admits trying to seduce Joseph and says he sought chastity; seeing their shared infatuation, she disclosed her desire and warned him she would persist.
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r3.anchor: وذكرت لهن أنها راودته لكنه اخذ بالعفة وطلب العصمة

TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r4.claim: Her threat uses oath-like emphasis, the emphatic nūn, and the lām to show settled resolve; it both asserts herself before the women and warns Joseph.
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r4.anchor: وقد أكدت الكلام بوجوه من التأكيد كالقسم والنون واللام

TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r5.claim: This threat is harsher than her earlier one: she now combines prison with humiliation and threatens directly, whereas before she asked her husband to choose prison or painful punishment.
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r5.anchor: أشد وأهول مما سألته زوجها يوم المراودة

TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r6.claim: Her earlier threat offered prison or painful punishment, while this one combines prison and being made low.
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r6.anchor: رددت الجزاء هناك بين السجن والعذاب الأليم وجمع ههنا بين الجزاءين

TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r7.claim: Threatening Joseph herself rather than petitioning her husband presents her as decisive and shows her power to redirect her husband’s will.
TABATABAI:12:32-33#2/r7.anchor: قامت بالتهديد بنفسها لا بأن تسأل زوجها

TABATABAI:12:35/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:35/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:35/r3.claim: The signs of Joseph’s innocence include the child’s testimony, his shirt torn from behind, the pair racing to the door, and perhaps the women’s amazement and the wife’s admission.
TABATABAI:12:35/r3.anchor: الشواهد والأدلة الدالة على براءة يوسف عليه السلام وطهارة ذيله

TABATABAI:12:35/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:35/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:35/r6.claim: Later evidence shows the wife may have misled her husband into doubting Joseph’s innocence; she may have arranged or ordered prison both to protect herself and to punish him into obedience.
TABATABAI:12:35/r6.anchor: فقد كان سجنه بتوسل أو بأمر منها لتدفع بذلك تهمة الناس عن نفسها

TABRISI:12:30-35#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:30-35#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:30-35#2/r8.claim: Al-ṣāghirūn denotes people in humiliation and disgrace; ṣabā is the heart's tenderness and inclination.
TABRISI:12:30-35#2/r8.anchor: والصاغرين من الصغار صغر بصغر صغارا وهو الذل والهوان والصبا رقة القلب

THALABI:v5p219/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p219/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p219/r6.claim: The wife tells the women that this is the man whose love they blamed her for, admits seducing him, and says he resisted; she threatens prison and humiliation if he disobeys.
THALABI:v5p219/r6.anchor: ولقد راودته عن نفسه فاستعصم أي امتنع واستعصى

THALABI:v5p219/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p219/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p219/r7.claim: The emphatic nūn in the threat is heavy in the first verb and light in the second; at pause the light nūn is written with alif, as in another Quran phrase and al-Aʿsha’s verse.
THALABI:v5p219/r7.anchor: والوقف على قوله: ليسجنن بالنون لكنها مشددة. وعلى قوله: وليكونا بالألف لأنها مخففة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Zelicha felt relief at the other women’s humiliation, but then turned the failed lustful pursuit toward revenge; as a powerful official’s wife, she could send her slave to prison.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Failure of love in its lust induces it to revenge. It seems that in those times masters had unlimited powers over their slaves.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r1.claim: The fāʾ in fa-dhālikunna is explanatory; the demonstrative points to Joseph as a man of beauty beyond human ranks, or to the one whose sight made the women cut their hands.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r1.anchor: الفاء فصيحة والخطاب للنسوة والإشارة حسبما يقتضيه الظاهر إلى يوسف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r2.claim: The demonstrative and relative clause mean that this is the noble angel or the man they saw, cut their hands for, and blamed her for loving.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r2.anchor: فذلكن الملك الكريم الخارج في الحسن عن المراتب البشرية أو الذي قطعتن أيديكن بسببه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r3.claim: An alternative takes the demonstrative as the Canaanite slave the women had imagined; after seeing him, they know whom they blamed her for loving.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r3.anchor: العبد الكنعاني الذي صورتن في أنفسكن ثم لمتنني فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r4.claim: Another explanation says they had not pictured Joseph truly; if they had seen his real beauty, they would have excused her infatuation.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r4.anchor: لو صورتنه بما عاينتن لعذرتنني في الافتتان به

ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r5.claim: A distant demonstrative for a present person can exalt his beauty and mark his rarity; it may reflect his absence at the earlier blame, while the idea he was kept away now to prevent temptation is remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r5.anchor: رفعا لمنزلته في الحسن واستبعادا لمحله فيه وإشارة إلى أنه لغرابته بعيد أن يوجد مثله

ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows the demonstrative to refer to love of Joseph, with the pronoun in fīhi returning to that love; al-Ālūsī finds this remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r6.anchor: وجوز ابن عطية كون الإشارة إلى حب يوسف عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r7.claim: The wife confesses the remainder of her secret after establishing her case before the women; they had now experienced the attraction that affected her.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r7.anchor: وهو إباحة منها ببقية سرها بعد أن أقامت عليهن الحجة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya glosses istaʿṣama as seeking and holding fast to protection, and disobeying her.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r8.anchor: أي طلب العصمة وتمسك بها وعصاني

ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r9.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r9.claim: Al-Kashshāf says the intensive form istaʿṣama conveys emphatic refusal and strenuous self-restraint, like istamsaka and istawsaʿa.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p232/r9.anchor: وفي الكشاف أن الاستعصام بناءا مبالغة يدل على الامتناع البليغ

ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r1.speaker: الصوفيون
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r1.claim: The mystics say istaʿṣama is equivalent to iʿtaṣama, meaning he refrained from what she wanted; other forms similarly match iftiʿāl in meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r1.anchor: أنه موافق لإعتصم وأما استمسك واستوسع واستجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r2.claim: The word ʿiṣma here means lexical restraint, not the later technical meaning of divine protection from inclination to sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r2.anchor: وليس المراد بالعصمة ما أودعه الله تعالى في بعض أنبيائه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r3.claim: Another explanation takes istaʿṣama as his flight: Joseph first refused verbally, then fled when speech did not stop her, seeking protection through escape.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r3.anchor: قيل : وعنث بذلك فراره عليه السلام منها فإنه امتنع منها أولا بالمقال

ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r4.claim: Although the women already knew she tried to seduce him, she swears to her confession to show her delight in admitting it.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r4.anchor: مما تحدث به النسوة لإظهار ابتهاجها بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r5.claim: Another explanation says the oath especially emphasizes Joseph's refusal because youth, closeness, and her pressure made resistance seem unlikely; al-Ālūsī calls this unpersuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r5.anchor: وقيل : إنه باعتبار المعطوف وهو الاستعصام كأنها نظمته لقوة الداعي إلى خلافه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects that rationale as unconvincing and says the verse proves Joseph did not commit the scandalous act attributed by storytellers, rebuking al-Suddī for the tale of his undressing.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r6.anchor: وفي الآية دليل على أنه عليه السلام لم يصدر منه ما سود به القصاص وجوه الطروس

ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r7.claim: In mā āmuruhu, mā is relative and its preposition is omitted; the object of āmara may be left implicit or inferred from yufʿal, with other staged analyses of the pronouns.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r7.anchor: فما موصولة والجملة بعدها صلة والعائد الهاء وقد حذف حرف الجر منه فاتصل بالفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r8.claim: The cited poetic line illustrates the common omission of the preposition after āmara; her expression 'what I command' displays her assumed authority.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p233/r8.anchor: وهذا أمر شائع مع أمر كقوله : أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به

ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r1.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r1.claim: Ibn al-Munīr says the omitted preposition has become conventional, so the pronoun should be treated as an unattached accusative; two pronouns of the same type cannot attach together.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r1.anchor: إن هذا الجار مما أنس حذفه فلا يقدر العائد إلا منصوبا مفصولا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r2.claim: Mā may instead be a verbal noun, with the pronoun referring to Joseph; carrying out an order means doing what it entails, by figurative attribution or an implied noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ( ما ) مصدرية فالضمير المذكور ليوسف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r3.claim: She describes her solicitation as an order to display her assumed authority; li-yusjananna has a heavy nūn and passive form, fitting royal usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r3.anchor: وعبرت عن مراودتها بالأمر إظهار لجريان حكومتها عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r4.claim: The passive may also suggest imprisonment will follow immediately, as though no agent intervenes between her command and its execution.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r4.anchor: إيهاما لسرعة ترتب ذلك على عدم امتثاله لأمرها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r5.claim: Al-ṣāghirīn means the humiliated and lowly; ṣaghar describes rank, while ṣaghura concerns bodily size, with several verbal nouns reported.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r5.anchor: أي الأذلال المهانين وهو من صغر كفرح ومصدر صغر بفتحتين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r6.claim: One view says the heavy nūn emphasizes certain imprisonment while a light nūn marks uncertain humiliation; another says humiliation follows imprisonment, so light emphasis suffices.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r6.anchor: قيل : لتحققه وما بعده بالنون الخفيفة لأنه غير متحقق

ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r7.speaker: فرقة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r7.claim: A group read both verbs with heavy nūn, contrary to the written form; the alif represents the pause form, as in al-Aʿshā's cited line.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r7.anchor: وقرأت فرقة بالتثقيل فيهما وهو مخالف لرسم المصحف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r8.claim: One view says she earlier threatened painful punishment while angry and denying her advances, but now hopes to excuse herself, so she threatens prison; other views compare humiliation with the earlier torment, and the joined penalties here may be harsher.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r8.anchor: قيل : ولم تذكر العذاب الأليم الذي ذكرته في ( ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r9.claim: She intensifies the threat before the women to vent anger at Joseph's steadfastness and show him she fears no one, limiting their ability to advise him to comply.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p234/r9.anchor: ولعلها إنما بالغت في ذلك بمحضر من تلك النسوة لمزيد غيظها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r1.claim: The wife points to Joseph as the one for whose love the women blamed her, admits soliciting him, and threatens prison and humiliation if he refuses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r1.anchor: {فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه} أي: في حبه، ثم صرحت بما فعلت، فقالت: {ولقد راودته عن نفسه فاستعصم}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r2.claim: She assumes the women will not blame her after experiencing Joseph’s beauty; they urge him to obey his mistress.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r2.anchor: وإنما صرحت به لأنها علمت أنه لا ملامة عليها منهن وقد أصابهن ما أصابها من رؤيته،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r3.claim: The heavy emphatic nūn in layusjananna remains at pause, while the light nūn in walayakūnan pauses with alif, as in 96:15–16.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r3.anchor: والوقف على قوله: {ليسجنن} بالنون لأنها مشددة، وعلى قوله {"وليكونا "} بالألف لأنها مخففة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r4.claim: Joseph chose prison rather than committing the sin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p238#2/r4.anchor: فاختار يوسف عليه السلام السجن على المعصية حين توعدته المرأة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r1.claim: Dhalik may identify the Canaanite slave they censured before seeing him fully, implying they would excuse her if they had; alternatively that demonstrative elevates him by standing for this.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r1.anchor: أي فهو ذلك العبد الكنعاني الذي لمتنني في الافتنان به قبل أن تتصورنه حق تصوره، ولو تصورتنه بما عاينتن

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r2.claim: She admits soliciting Joseph once she sees the women excuse her, hoping they will help soften his resolve.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r2.anchor: أقرت لهن حين عرفت أنهن يعذرنها كي يعاونها على إلانة عريكته.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r3.claim: What I command may omit a preposition from what I command him, or mean the requirement of my command, with the pronoun referring to Joseph.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r3.anchor: أي ما آمر به، فحذف الجار أو أمري إياه بمعنى موجب أمري فيكون الضمير ليوسف.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r4.claim: The small ones means the humiliated; a variant ليكونن conflicts with the written codex, which writes nūn with alif according to pause spelling of the light nūn, similar to tanwin.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:32/r4.anchor: من الإذلاء وهو من صغر بالكسر يصغر صغرا وصغارا والصغير من صغر بالضم صغرا. وقرىء «ليكونن»

QASHANI:12:31-32/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:31-32/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:31-32/r4.claim: As the soul's contest over the heart's intention subsides and it learns to comply, the heart can enter seclusion, shedding attachments and indecision so its resolve becomes unified.
QASHANI:12:31-32/r4.anchor: بتردد العزم بانجذابه إلى جهة النفس تارة وإلى جهة الروح أخرى

QASHANI:12:31-32/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:31-32/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:31-32/r5.claim: This is discipline of the heart, which sheds its own attributes, knowledge, perfections, and unveilings in seeking annihilation and vision; it differs from training the soul through resistance, worship, and asceticism.
QASHANI:12:31-32/r5.anchor: إنما هي رياضة القلب بالتنزه عن صفاته وعلومه وكمالاته وكشوفه

QASHANI:12:31-32/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:31-32/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:31-32/r6.claim: The soul's threat means that, unless Joseph gives it its share, it will deprive him of bodily pleasure and sensory perception by retreat and humble him by stripping his rank among the body's servants.
QASHANI:12:31-32/r6.anchor: من إيفاء حظي ليمنعن من اللذات البدنية وروح الهوى والمدركات الحسية

QASHANI:12:31-32/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:31-32/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:31-32/r7.claim: Joseph's longing for seclusion resembles the Prophet's inclination to retreat for worship at Hira.
QASHANI:12:31-32/r7.anchor: كما حببت إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عند التحنث في حراء

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam recounts that the women cut their fingers while slicing citron, felt no pain from Joseph's beauty, and then agreed the wife had no blame after seeing him.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r1.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم قال : واعتدت لهن متكئا قال : لما تغدين ، وطابت انفسهن

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi recounts the women cutting citron, calling Joseph no human but a noble angel, after which the wife says he is the one they blamed her for.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r2.anchor: عن السدي : وقالت ليوسف اخرج عليهن ، فلما خرج راى النسوة يوسف

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses Joseph's response fāstaʿṣama as resisting or refraining.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : فاستعصم يقول : فامتنع

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r4.claim: Qatada explains fāstaʿṣama as fāstaʿṣā, meaning he resisted.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة ، قوله : فاستعصم اي : فاستعصى

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says Joseph had loosened his trousers, then something made him stop, though the report does not know what changed.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r5.anchor: عن السدي ، ولقد راودته ، عن نفسه فاستعصم بعدما كان قد حل سراويله

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr glosses the threatened humiliation as being made low or disgraced.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2137#2/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : صاغرين يعني : مذلين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r1.claim: The fa in ‘that is he’ is explanatory: if Yusuf is as you claim an angel, he is the man for whom you blamed me.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r2.claim: Fi in ‘you blamed me over him’ is causal, with an omitted noun meaning the matter or love of him; a hadith uses the same causal fi.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r2.anchor: ( في ) للتعليل ، مثل ( دخلت امرأة النار في هرة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r3.claim: Dhalikunna distinguishes Yusuf, whom the women had not seen; the relative phrase identifies him by the only description they knew, and she admitted pursuing him once she saw their infatuation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r3.anchor: والإشارة ب ( ذلكن ) لتمييز يوسف عليه السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r4.claim: Istaʿṣama is an intensive form meaning Yusuf strongly protected himself, as with other verbs formed using s and t.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r4.anchor: فالسين والتاء للمبالغة ، مثل : استمسك واستجمع الرأي واستجاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r5.claim: He refused as one protected from sin, treating the woman’s advances as wrongdoing from which he guarded himself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r5.anchor: أنه امتنع امتناع معصوم ، أي جاعلا المراودة خطيئة عصم نفسه منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r6.claim: She remained intent on seduction, asserted her status and command, and emphasized the prison threat with the nuns to frighten Yusuf in his hearing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r6.anchor: فأكدت حصول سجنه بنوني التوكيد ، وقد قالت ذلك بمسمع منه إرهابا له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r7.claim: The relative clause in ma amuruhu omits a pronoun governed by bi through removal of the preposition, as in amartuka al-khayr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r7.anchor: وحذف عائد صلة { ما آمره } وهو ضمير مجرور بالباء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r8.claim: With fatḥa, sijn is the regular verbal noun for imprisonment and is attested by Ibn ʿĀshūr only in Yaʿqub’s reading here; with kasra it names the prison building.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r8.anchor: ولم أره في كلامهم بفتح السين إلا في قراءة يعقوب هذه الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r9.claim: Saghir means humiliated; min al-saghirin is stronger than simply calling Yusuf humiliated, as shown in two earlier verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p263/r9.anchor: وتركيب من الصاغرين } أقوى في معنى الوصف بالصغار من أن يقال

AKHFASH:v1p397/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p397/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p397/r2.claim: At a pause, light nūn after an open vowel becomes a still alif, so وليكونا is paused as وليكونا; the same applies to لنسفعا.
AKHFASH:v1p397/r2.anchor: وقال {وليكونا من الصاغرين} فالوقف علهيا (وليكونا) لان النون الخفيفة اذا انفتح ما قبلها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p438/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p438/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p438/r13.claim: Istiʿṣām is an intensive form for emphatic resistance and careful self-protection, as if Joseph were already chaste and striving to increase that protection; it proves his innocence.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p438/r13.anchor: الاستعصام : بناء مبالغة يدل على الامتناع البليغ والتحفظ الشديد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p438/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p438/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p438/r14.claim: In the phrase “my command,” the pronoun refers to the relative clause: “what I command,” with the preposition omitted; alternatively mā is a verbal noun and refers to Joseph’s response to her command.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p438/r14.anchor: بل إلى الموصول . والمعنى : ما آمر به ، فحذف الجار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p438/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p438/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p438/r15.claim: The verb wa-layakūnan is read with either a doubled or light nūn; the light nūn is preferred because the muṣḥaf writes it as an alif of pause.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p438/r15.anchor: قرىء : ( وليكونا ) بالتشديد والتخفيف . والتخفيف أولى

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#2/r1.claim: Fa-staʿṣama means he refused or restrained himself.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r1.claim: Rael says Joseph is the man for whom they blamed her: had they pictured his beauty correctly, they would excuse her fascination.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r1.anchor: تقول هو ذلك العبد الكنعانى الذى صورتن فى أنفسكهن ثم لمتننى فيه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r2.claim: Istiʿṣāma is an intensive form for powerful resistance and vigilance; her admission plainly confirms Joseph’s innocence of the alleged inclination and proof.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r2.anchor: والإستعصام بناء مبالغة يدل على الامتناع البليغ والتحفظ الشديد

NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r3.claim: She threatens imprisonment and humiliation if Joseph will not do what she commands; the final alif substitutes for the light nun of emphasis.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r3.anchor: والضمير يرجع إلى يوسف أى ولئن لم يفعل أمرى إياه أى موجب احري ومقتضاه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r4.claim: Her threat depicts Joseph as lowly with thieves and fugitives, unable to eat, drink, or sleep; she says the man who rejected silk and a princely couch will end desolate on coarse matting.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#2/r4.anchor: ليحبسن والألف فى ﴿ وليكون ﴾ بدل من نون التأكيد الخفيفة ﴿ من الصاغرين ﴾ مع السراق والسفاك والأباق

QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r5.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r5.claim: When the women were captivated, the wife defended herself: ذلك means this, and what they blamed her for was loving him.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r6.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to love and ذلك keeps its usual sense: that love is what they blamed her for.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r6.anchor: وقيل: الهاء للحب، و«ذلك» على بابه، والمعنى: ذلكن الحب

QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r7.claim: Lawm means describing someone with an ugly or blameworthy quality.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r7.anchor: واللوم الوصف بالقبيح. ثم أقرت وقالت:

QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r8.claim: The wife admits seducing Yusuf; استعصم means he refrained, and عصمة is named for preventing sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r8.anchor: أي امتنع وسميت العصمة عصمة لأنها تمنع من ارتكاب المعصية.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r9.claim: استعصم may instead be understood as استعصى, with the same meaning.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r10.claim: She renews the seduction in front of the women and threatens prison now that she no longer fears blame, unlike her initial private approach.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r10.anchor: عاودته المراودة بمحضر منهن، وهتكت جلباب الحياء

QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r11.claim: The الصاغرين are the humiliated and abased.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r12.claim: The codex writes وليكونا with alif; it is read with a light emphatic nūn, while ليسجنن has the heavy nūn.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r12.anchor: وخط المصحف «وليكونا» بالألف وتقرأ بنون مخففة للتأكيد

QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r13.claim: A light emphatic nūn is written with pausal alif, as in 96:15 and al-A'sha's line.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:31-32/r13.anchor: ونحوها الوقف عليها بالألف، كقول الأعشى:

QURTUBI-FULL:12:30-32/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:30-32/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:30-32/r1.claim: The poet intended a form ending in light emphatic nūn; when paused, it is written with alif as فاعبدا.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:30-32/r1.anchor: فلما وقف عليه كان الوقف بالألف.

RAZI-FULL:v18p102#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p102#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p102#2/r1.claim: The women can excuse the wife's love because Joseph's beauty invited passion while his angelic conduct made access seem impossible, bringing longing and distress.
RAZI-FULL:v18p102#2/r1.anchor: فحسنه يوجب الحب الشديد وسيرته الملكية توجب اليأس عن الوصول إليه

RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r1.claim: The women had condemned her love, but after one glance they suffered greater shock than she had during her long time with Joseph, so she says they deserved blame.
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r1.anchor: لأنهن بنظرة واحدة لحقهن أعظم مما نالها مع أنه طال مكثه عندها

RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says ذلك points to Joseph after he had left the gathering.
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري : أشارت بصيغة ذلكن إلى يوسف بعد انصرافه من المجلس

RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r3.claim: The Kashshaf's explanation, which Razi calls best, is that she identifies the handsome man as the Canaanite slave they blamed her for loving, showing they had not imagined his beauty.
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r3.anchor: وهو الذي ذكره صاحب ( الكشاف ) وهو أحسن ما قيل

RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r4.claim: Her admission that she pursued him and he resisted explicitly establishes Joseph's innocence of the accusation.
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r4.anchor: واعلم أن هذا تصريح بأنه عليه السلام كان بريئا عن تلك التهمة

RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r5.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says Joseph only resisted after the garment was removed; Razi rejects this as a corrupt addition unsupported by the text.
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r5.anchor: وعن السدي أنه قال : { فاستعصم } بعد حل السراويل

RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r6.claim: Razi asks what could justify attaching this false, corrupt addition to the scriptural text.
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r6.anchor: وما الذي يحمله على إلحاق هذه الزيادة الفاسدة الباطلة بنص الكتاب

RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r7.claim: The threat means that if Joseph refused her demand, she would imprison and humiliate him, a threat with strong effect on someone high-minded.
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r7.anchor: والمراد أن يوسف عليه السلام إن لم يوافقها على مرادها يوقع في السجن وفي الصغار

RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r8.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r8.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i pause on وليكونا with the alif, as they do on the cited word in Surat al-Alaq.
RAZI-FULL:v18p104#2/r8.anchor: كان حمزة والكسائي يقفان على { وليكونا } بالألف

STUDYQURAN:12:32/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:32/r1.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:12:32/r1.claim: Zulaykhā implies that the women could not withstand one glimpse of Joseph, so she could not be blamed for living with him constantly; she admits her fault and his innocence.
STUDYQURAN:12:32/r1.anchor: since the women could not even withstand the sight of Joseph for one moment without losing their senses

STUDYQURAN:12:32/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:32/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:32/r2.claim: Her command refers back to her original demand that Joseph lie with her.
STUDYQURAN:12:32/r2.anchor: her original command to Joseph to lie with her

TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r1.claim: The Aziz’s wife says the women’s loss of reason and cutting their hands after seeing Yusuf is exactly what they had blamed her for in loving him; she admits she pursued him and he resisted.
TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r1.anchor: هو الذي لمتنني في حبي إياه، وشغف فؤادي به

TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r2.claim: He says Yusuf resisted after she had pulled down his trousers, adding that he does not know why Yusuf changed course.
TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r2.anchor: عن السدي، " {قالت فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه ولقد راودته عن نفسه فاستعصم} [يوسف: 32] : تقول: بعد ما حل السراويل

TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r3.claim: He glosses fastaʿṣama as he resisted.

TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r4.claim: He glosses fastaʿṣama as he refrained or refused.
TAB-FULL:v13p141#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {فاستعصم} [يوسف: 32] يقول: فامتنع "

TAB-FULL:v13p142/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p142/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p142/r1.claim: He cites the strengthened-nūn form liyubṭiʾanna as a parallel to pausing on the strengthened nūn of layusjananna.

TAB-FULL:v13p142/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p142/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p142/r2.claim: The light emphatic nūn in wa-layakūnanna is represented by alif at pause, like the light tanwīn-like ending in nouns.
TAB-FULL:v13p142/r2.anchor: فإن الوقف عليه بالألف؛ لأنها النون الخفيفة

TAB-FULL:v13p142/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p142/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p142/r3.claim: The same pause convention appears in la-nasfaʿan and in al-Aʿsha’s line, whose written ending represents faʿbadn.
TAB-FULL:v13p142/r3.anchor: ومنه قول الأعشى: [البحر الطويل] وصل على حين العشيات والضحى

TABATABAI:12:32/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:32/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:32/r1.claim: Akbarna means they regarded him with awe; the sudden sight of overwhelming beauty eclipsed their thoughts and intentions, explaining their confused cutting, while the intensive form suggests repeated cutting.
TABATABAI:12:32/r1.anchor: الإكبار الإعظام وهو كناية عن اندهاشهن وغيبتهن عن شعورهن وإرادتهن بمفاجأة مشاهدة ذاك الحسن الرائع

TABATABAI:12:32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:32/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:32/r2.claim: Beginning with “Glory be to God” before declaring Yusuf innocent follows the etiquette of first exalting God when speaking to exonerate someone; 24:16 offers a parallel.
TABATABAI:12:32/r2.anchor: فهن لما أردن تنزيهه عليه السلام بقولهن { ما هذا بشرا } الخ

TABATABAI:12:32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:32/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:32/r3.claim: Calling Yusuf a noble angel reflects their belief that angels are exalted sources of goodness, beauty, knowledge, and joy, imagined in ideal human forms; the phrase praises his inner and outer qualities.
TABATABAI:12:32/r3.anchor: وهذا بناء على ما يعتقده المليون منهم الوثنيون أن الملائكة موجودات شريفة هم مبادئ كل خير وسعادة في العالم

TABATABAI:12:32/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:32/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:32/r4.claim: The women did not initially mean to excuse the Azizah; their praise was involuntary, and she invoked their exposed actions and words only afterward to make them admit her point.
TABATABAI:12:32/r4.anchor: وتقدم قولهن هذا على قول امرأة العزيز { فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه } يدل على أنهن لم يفهمن بهذا الكلام إعذار لامرأة العزيز

SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r1.claim: فذلكن is a subject with the relative clause as predicate; the distant demonstrative exalts Yusuf and supports her defense of why she loved him.
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r1.anchor: أشارت إليه إشارة البعيد وإن كان حاضرا تعظيما له

SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r2.claim: He suggests ذلك points to Yusuf's love, with فيه referring to that love, so the demonstrative is literally distant.
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r2.anchor: وجوز ابن عطية أن يكون " ذلك "

SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r3.claim: The author clarifies that distant here means far, and says demonstrative reference is only to something present in any case.
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r3.anchor: قلت: يعني بالغائب البعيد، وإلا فالإشارة لا تكون إلا لحاضر

SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r4.claim: ما in ما آمره may be a verbal noun or a relative pronoun; if relative, it is the object of يفعل, and the hāʾ in آمره may refer to it or to Yusuf.
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r4.anchor: في " ما " وجهان، أحدهما: أنها مصدرية. والثاني: أنها موصولة،

SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r5.claim: He takes the hāʾ in آمره to refer to the relative pronoun, with a deleted preposition as in أمرتك الخير; if ما is a verbal noun, the hāʾ can refer to Yusuf and mean carrying out her command to him.
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r5.anchor: فإن قلت: الضمير في " آمره " راجع إلى الموصول أم إلى يوسف؟ قلت: بل إلى الموصول

SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r6.claim: Under the verbal-noun analysis, the first object is omitted: ما آمره به, with the pronoun referring to Yusuf.
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r6.anchor: المفعول الأول محذوف تقديره: ما آمره به وهو ضمير يوسف

SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r7.claim: He reads the sīn in استعصم as carrying its request force: the intensified pattern depicts strong refusal and strenuous seeking of protection, like استمسك، استوسع، استجمع، and استفحل.
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r7.anchor: الاستعصام بناء مبالغة يدل على الامتناع البليغ والتحفظ الشديد

SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r8.claim: He says Yusuf sought protection, held fast to it, and disobeyed her.

SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r9.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r9.claim: He prefers treating استعصم as equivalent to اعتصم, since اعتصم denotes achieved protection whereas seeking it need not succeed; the cited forms mostly match افتعل, while استفحل matches تفعّل.
SAMIN-DURR:12:32/r9.anchor: والذي ذكره التصريفيون في " استعصم " أنه موافق ل " اعتصم " فاستفعل فيه موافق

SAMIN-DURR:12:32#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:32#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:32#2/r1.claim: The common reading lightens the nūn of وليكونن; at pause it is written and pronounced with alif like tanwīn, while the restored nūn is the nominative nūn when nothing requires its deletion.
SAMIN-DURR:12:32#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ العامة بتخفيف نون " وليكونن " ، ويقفون عليها بالألف

SAMIN-DURR:12:32#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:32#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:32#2/r2.claim: A group reads the nūn doubled; the consonantal text's alif reflects the pause form, as in poetry where an emphatic nūn becomes alif and connected speech is treated like pause.
SAMIN-DURR:12:32#2/r2.anchor: وقرأت فرقة بتشديدها، وفيها مخالفة لسواد المصحف لكتبها فيه ألفا

SAMIN-DURR:12:32#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:32#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:32#2/r3.claim: The cited line والله فاعبدا represents فاعبدن with its final emphatic nūn replaced by alif at pause.
SAMIN-DURR:12:32#2/r3.anchor: أي: فاعبدن فأبدلها ألفا، وهو أحد الأقوال في قول امرىء القيس:

TABRISI:12:31/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:31/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:31/r6.claim: The light emphatic nūn marks an oath and becomes alif at pause, like tanwin in rajulan.
TABRISI:12:31/r6.anchor: هذه النون الخفيفة التي يتلقى بها القسم وإذا وقفت عليها وقفت بالألف

TABRISI:12:31/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:31/r7.speaker: الأعشى
TABRISI:12:31/r7.claim: Al-A'sha's faʿbudā stands for faʿbudanna, replacing the nūn by alif at pause.

TABRISI:12:31/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:31/r8.speaker: الشاعر
TABRISI:12:31/r8.claim: The line bada laka min tilka al-qalūsi badāʾ illustrates an implicit verbal noun serving as subject of bada lahum.
TABRISI:12:31/r8.anchor: بدا لك من تلك القلوص بداء

TABRISI:12:31#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:31#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:31#2/r1.claim: Layasjunannahu cannot be the grammatical subject of bada lahum because a full clause cannot serve as subject here.
TABRISI:12:31#2/r1.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون ليسجننه في موضع الفاعل لأن الجملة لا تكون فاعلا

TABRISI:12:31-32/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:31-32/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:31-32/r7.claim: The wife says this is the one the women blamed her for loving; their response after one sight excuses her daily love.
TABRISI:12:31-32/r7.anchor: جعلت إعظامهن إياه عذرا لها والمعنى هذا الذي أصابكن في رؤيته مرة واحدة

TABRISI:12:31-32/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:31-32/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:31-32/r8.claim: She admits pursuing him while he resisted; one view says he sought God's protection, confirming he committed no wrong.
TABRISI:12:31-32/r8.anchor: وقيل: معناه امتنع بالله وسأله العصمة من فعل القبيح

TABRISI:12:31-32/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:31-32/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:31-32/r9.claim: She threatens imprisonment and humiliation; Joseph chooses prison over sin.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r1.claim: In Arabic, blame is describing someone as blameworthy; its opposite is praise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r1.anchor: معنى اللوم في اللغة (¬1) الوصف بالقبيح، ونقيضه الحمد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r2.claim: The wife meant to justify herself before the women by showing them Joseph’s beauty, which stunned them and made them cut their hands.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r2.anchor: (أرادت امرأة العزيز إظهار عذرها عند النسوة، بما يشاهدن من جمال يوسف)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says “that is the one” points to Joseph after he had left the gathering.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r3.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري (¬4): أشارت بذلك إلى يوسف بعد انصرافه من المجلس،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas paraphrases the statement as: this is the man whose love and infatuation you blamed me for.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r4.anchor: ما روي أن ابن عباس (¬5) قال: في قوله {فذلكن} يريد فهو الذي لمتنني فيه، أي في حبه، والشغف به،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، المفسرون، أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r5.claim: “He sought protection” means Joseph refrained; the root denotes seeking protection or preventing an act.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬6) والمفسرون (¬7) وأهل اللغة (¬8): فامتنع، ومعنى الاستعصام الامتناع بطلب العصمة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r6.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r6.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says ʿiṣma means prevention in Arabic; God’s protecting a servant keeps him from ruin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r6.anchor: قال الأصمعي (¬9): العصمة في كلام العرب المنع، وعصمة الله العبد، أن يمنعه مما يوبقه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r7.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p105/r7.claim: Qatada transmits an alternative reading or wording, “fa-staʿṣā,” meaning he firmly resisted.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p106/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p106/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p106/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the wife’s command as what she was inviting Joseph to do; she threatens prison if he refuses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p106/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬2): يريد ما أدعوا إليه {ليسجنن} توعدته بإيقاع المكروه به،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p106/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p106/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p106/r2.claim: She threatens that refusal will make Joseph both imprisoned and humiliated; the weak and emphatic nūn forms are discussed elsewhere.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p106/r2.anchor: إن لم يطعها فيما تدعوه إليه، و {وليكونا من الصاغرين}، ومضى الكلام في النون الشديدة والخفيفة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p106/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p106/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p106/r3.claim: “The abased” means the humiliated; the author refers readers to the usage in 9:29.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p106/r3.anchor: والصاغر الذليل، ذكرنا ذلك في قوله {وهم صاغرون}

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:31-32/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:31-32/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:31-32/r9.claim: The Aziz's wife points out that Joseph is the one for whose love they blamed her, admits she tried to seduce him, and says he resisted.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:31-32/r9.anchor: { فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه } في حبه والشغف فيه، ثم أقرت عندهن بما فعلت فقالت: { ولقد راودته عن نفسه فاستعصم }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:31-32/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:31-32/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:31-32/r10.claim: She threatens imprisonment; the women urge Joseph to obey her and falsely present him as the oppressor and her as wronged.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:31-32/r10.anchor: وتوعدته بالسجن فقالت: { ولئن لم يفعل... } الآية؛ فأمرنه بطاعتها، وقلن له: إنك الظالم وهي المظلومة

ELMALILI:12:30-32/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:12:30-32/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:12:30-32/r1.claim: Yusuf’s chastity and purity are evident from his resistance under this coercion and threat.
ELMALILI:12:30-32/r1.anchor: Yûsuf’un ismet ve nezâhetini anlamalı ki böyle bir ikrah ve tehdid karşısında

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:30/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:30/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:30/r2.claim: Zeliha openly admitted desiring Joseph, praised his chastity, and threatened imprisonment if he refused her.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:30/r2.anchor: Ben onunla birlikte olmak istedim. Fakat o, iffetini korudu. Andolsun, eğer kendisinden istediğimi yapmazsa mutlaka zindana atılacak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:30/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:30/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:30/r3.claim: Zeliha used the banquet to argue that loving such a handsome slave was no social disgrace, despite the women's condemnation of her attempted adultery.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:30/r3.anchor: böyle yakışıklı ve güzel bir köleye âşık olmanın, toplum değerleri açısından, kendisi için bir nakîsa olmadığını vurgulamak istemiştir

ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r2.claim: The Qur'anic episodes in 12:26-34 are absent from Genesis, where the husband immediately believes the accusation and imprisons Joseph.
ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r2.anchor: the Qur'anic narrative differs from the story as told in the Bible

ASAD-NOTES:12:32#n30/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:32#n30/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:32#n30/r1.claim: The phrase literally means "become one of those who are humiliated."
ASAD-NOTES:12:32#n30/r1.anchor: Lit., "become one of those who are humiliated"

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p420/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p420/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p420/r1.claim: The reading of hayta as “I prepared myself for you” conflicts with the dialogue: on that interpretation she would say hayta lī, so the report is mistaken.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p420/r1.anchor: ولو كان على هذه الرواية لقالت له: هيت لي، فالوهم في هذه الرواية ظاهر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p271/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p271/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p271/r6.claim: The plural demonstrative’s kāf addresses the women, and its distant form may signal her wish to keep them away after their disturbance and cutting their hands.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p271/r6.anchor: ذا اسم الإشارة، واللام لبعد المشار، وكن خطاب لتلك النسوة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p271/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p271/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p271/r7.claim: One possible reading is that she points to Joseph as distant to prevent the women’s temptation from growing and let them recover their composure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p271/r7.anchor: واحتمل أن يكون لما رأى دهشهن وتقطيع أيديهن بالسكاكين وقولهن: ما هذا بشرا، بعد عنهن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p271/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p271/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p271/r8.claim: Alternatively, the distant demonstrative magnifies Joseph’s beauty and expresses how extraordinary and remote his station seems.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p271/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون أشارت إليه وهو للبعد قريب بلفظ البعيد رفعا لمنزلته في الحسن

RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.claim: A verb is an expression indicating that an action occurs to an unspecified thing at an unspecified time; the explicit thing is its subject.
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.anchor: الفعل لفظة مفردة دالة على حصول المصدر لشيء غير معين في زمان غير معين

RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r2.claim: The grammatical subject is broader than an intentional agent: the action occurs to a subject in both قام and the involuntary مات.
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r2.anchor: حصل المصدر له أعم من قولنا بإيجاده واختياره كقولنا قام أو لا باختياره كقولنا مات

RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r3.claim: A verb form requires its action to occur to a subject, not an object; intransitive verbs show that an object is not required.
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r3.anchor: صيغة الفعل من حيث هي تقتضي حصول ذلك المصدر لشيء ما هو الفاعل ولا تقتضي حصوله للمفعول

RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r4.claim: The verb precedes its subject conceptually and in expression because understanding an action entails something to which the mind assigns it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r4.anchor: فحصول ماهية الفعل في الذهن يستلزم حصول شيء يسند الذهن ذلك الفعل إليه

RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r5.claim: In ضرب زيد the mind first posits an unspecified subject then identifies it as Zayd; in زيد ضرب, Zayd is the topic and the clause is its predicate.
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r5.anchor: إذا قلنا ضرب زيد فقد حكم الذهن بإسناد مفهوم ضرب إلى شيء ثم يحكم الذهن بأن ذلك الشيء هو زيد

RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r6.claim: Grammarians treat the subject as part of the verb but not the object, arguing from the form ضربت and from the ability to leave the object separate as in ضربك.
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r6.anchor: كقولهم ضربك وذلك يدل على أنهم اعتقدوا أن الفاعل جزء من الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r7.claim: A second argument that the subject is integral is the subject pronoun in الزيدان قاما; by the same rule, Zayd struck contains an implicit subject pronoun.
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r7.anchor: الزيدان قاما أظهرت الضمير للفاعل وكذلك إذا قلت زيد ضرب وجب أن يكون الفعل مسند إلى الضمير المستكن

RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r8.claim: Conceptually, ضرب means striking occurred to something in the past, so that something is part of the verb's meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r8.anchor: مفهوم قولك ضرب هو أنه حصل الضرب لشيء ما في زمان مضى فذلك الشيء الذي حصل له الضرب

RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r9.claim: The well-known rule disallows an antecedent pronoun in ضرب غلامه زيدا: غلامه is raised by ضرب and occupies its place, so its pronoun precedes its antecedent.
RAZI-FULL:v1p54#2/r9.anchor: والمشهور أنه لا يجوز لأنك رفعت غلامه بضرب فكان واقعا موقعة والشيء إذا وقع موقعه لم تجز إزالته عنه

BAQILLANI:v1p219/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r1.claim: Bāqillānī examines al-Buḥturī’s poems as he did Imruʾ al-Qays’s, to teach readers how to assess comparison, similarity, and degrees of likeness.
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r1.anchor: ونحن نعمد إلى بعض قصائد البحتري فنتكلم عليها كما تكلمنا على قصيدة امرئ القيس ليزداد الناظر في كتابنا بصيرة

BAQILLANI:v1p219/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r2.speaker: البحتري
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r2.claim: Al-Buḥturī said his finest poem was the one beginning “Welcome to that approaching apparition.”
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r2.anchor: سمعت البحتري يذكر أن أجود شعر قاله

BAQILLANI:v1p219/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r3.speaker: أبو الفضل بن العميد
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r3.claim: Ibn al-ʿAmīd judged al-Buḥturī’s finest line to be “In gray hair is a warning, if only it would heed.”
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r3.anchor: قال وسمعت أبا الفضل بن العميد يقول أجود شعره هو قوله

BAQILLANI:v1p219/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r4.claim: Asked to choose, Bāqillānī defers to al-Buḥturī’s own judgment because a poet knows his poetry better than others.
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r4.anchor: وسئلت عن ذلك فقلت البحتري أعرف بشعر نفسه من غيره

BAQILLANI:v1p219/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r5.claim: The phrase “that apparition” is heavy, overlong, and padded; al-Ṣanawbarī’s lighter wording is better.
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r5.anchor: البيت الأول في قوله ذلكم الخيال ثقل روح وتطويل وحشو وغيره أصلح له وأخف منه قول الصنوبري

BAQILLANI:v1p219/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r6.claim: A single added or omitted letter can turn sweetness into harshness, eloquence into awkwardness, and ease into strained complexity.
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r6.anchor: وعذوبة الشعر تذهب بزيادة حرف أو نقصان حرف فيصير إلى الكزازة وتعود ملاحته بذلك ملوحة

BAQILLANI:v1p219/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r7.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r7.claim: Greeting an apparition works when addressed as it arrives; recounting its past arrival as though present creates a syntactic and semantic difficulty.
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r7.anchor: وفيه شيء آخر وهو أن هذا الخطاب إنما يستقيم مهما خوطب به

BAQILLANI:v1p219/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r8.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r8.claim: “Whether he did what we desire or not” is neither graceful nor elegant diction.
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r8.anchor: ليست بكلمة رشيقة ولا لفظة ظريفة وإن كانت كسائر الكلام

BAQILLANI:v1p219/r9.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r9.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r9.claim: The second line, about lightning crossing Wajra and guiding lost camel-riders, is splendid in effect, approach, appearance, and sound.
BAQILLANI:v1p219/r9.anchor: فأما بيته الثاني فهو عظيم الموقع في البهجة وبديع المأخذ حسن الرواء أنيق المنظر والمسمع

BURHAN:v4p428/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p428/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p428/r8.claim: The heavy emphatic nūn is used for imprisonment but not the following clause to magnify the threat of imprisonment.
BURHAN:v4p428/r8.anchor: من حيث أكدت السجن بالشدة دون ما بعده إعظاما

BURHAN:v4p302/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p302/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p302/r4.claim: In the women’s statement about Joseph, في carries a causal sense: “for this you blamed me.”

BURHAN:v3p108#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r1.claim: Reason establishes an omitted word when speech would otherwise be impossible, as when a command to ask a town means to ask its people.
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r1.anchor: فمنها أن يدل عليه العقل حيث تستحيل صحة الكلام عقلا إلا بتقدير محذوف

BURHAN:v3p108#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r2.claim: Sharia usage supplies an omitted act in prohibitions of the dead: legal permissibility applies to consuming the corpse, not the entity itself; the author rejects al-Talkhis’s appeal to reason.
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r2.anchor: فإن الذات لا تتصف بالحل والحرمة شرعا إنما هما من صفات الأفعال الواقعة على الذوات

BURHAN:v3p108#2/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r3.claim: Reason indicates ellipsis in وجاء ربك because bodily coming is a mark of created things; the author supplies God’s command or similar, while al-Zamakhshari treats it as a likeness to a king arriving without ellipsis.
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r3.anchor: لأن العقل دل على أصل الحذف ولاستحالة مجيء البارىء عقلا لأن المجيء من سمات الحدوث

BURHAN:v3p108#2/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r4.claim: In the monotheism argument, no corruption entails that there are not multiple gods; the omitted premise follows because denying a necessary consequence denies its cause.
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r4.anchor: لأنه في معرض التوحيد فعدم الفساد دليل على عدم تعدد الآلهة وإنما حذف لأن انتفاء اللازم يستلزم انتفاء الملزوم

BURHAN:v3p108#2/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r5.claim: Reason shows an omitted circumstance in فذلكن الذي لمتنني فيه because Joseph is not a place for blame; custom selects the deliberate seduction rather than love, which overwhelms its subject.
BURHAN:v3p108#2/r5.anchor: فإن يوسف عليه السلام ليس ظرفا للومهن فتعين أن يكون غيره فقد دل العقل على أصل الحذف

BURHAN:v3p44/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p44/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p44/r1.claim: Oaths intensify emphasis; sometimes إي is added, while the oath verb and preposition may be omitted when the answer makes them clear, as in the threat to imprison Joseph.
BURHAN:v3p44/r1.anchor: قد علمت أن القسم إنما جيء به لتوكيد المقسم عليه فتارة يزيدون فيه للمبالغة في التوكيد

BURHAN:v3p44/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p44/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p44/r2.claim: The oath answer may be omitted while the oath remains, as in ص والقرآن ذي الذكر; proposed answers are a threat of punishment for unbelief or إن ذلك لحق.
BURHAN:v3p44/r2.anchor: على أحد الأقوال أن الجواب حذف لطول الكلام وتقديره لأعذبنهم على كفرهم

BURHAN:v3p44/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p44/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p44/r3.claim: Other abbreviated oaths omit the sworn-by object, interpret testimony as swearing, or omit lām and qad from the response; the first الحق is an oath and the second confirms it.
BURHAN:v3p44/r3.anchor: لأن الشهادة بمعنى اليمين بدليل قوله

BURHAN:v3p44/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p44/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
BURHAN:v3p44/r4.claim: Al-Farisi divides oath-like expressions into those lacking a response, which may be oath or circumstantial, and those connected to an oath response.
BURHAN:v3p44/r4.anchor: قال الفارسي في الحجة الألفاظ الجارية مجرى القسم ضربان أحدهما ما تكون جارية كغيرها من الأخبار

BURHAN:v2p202/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p202/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p202/r1.claim: Knowledge of a verse’s occasion of revelation is a major aid to understanding; the Companions and early generations relied on it.
BURHAN:v2p202/r1.anchor: السادس معرفة النزول وهو من أعظم المعين على فهم المعنى وسبق منه في أول الكتاب جملة

BURHAN:v2p377/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p377/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p377/r1.claim: The two negations differ: one denies a specific direct act without establishing whether another person acted; the other denies that the subject did it and implies someone else did.
BURHAN:v2p377/r1.anchor: احدهما ان الاولى نفت ضربا خاص وهو ضرك اياه ولم تدل على وقوع ضرب غيرك ولا عدمه

BURHAN:v2p377/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p377/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p377/r2.claim: Negation scope depends on word order: negation before a general term denies the universal, whereas the general term before negation denies all instances and conflicts with a particular affirmation.
BURHAN:v2p377/r2.anchor: اذا كان الكلام عاما ونفيته فان تقدم حرف النفي اداة العموم كان نفيا للعموم

BURHAN:v2p377/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p377/r3.speaker: عبد القاهر
BURHAN:v2p377/r3.claim: ʿAbd al-Qahir says negating the whole entails that some was done; the author rejects this, saying denial of universality entails neither universal negation nor a particular positive.
BURHAN:v2p377/r3.anchor: وحكى الامام في نهاية الايجاز عن الشيخ عبد القاهر ان نفي العموم يقتضي خصوص الاثبات

BURHAN:v2p377/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p377/r4.speaker: الخوي
BURHAN:v2p377/r4.claim: Al-Khuyi derives four basic negation particles from lā and mā: mā and lā pair with past and future, while lam and lan pair by form with future and past; their letters and order reflect those origins.
BURHAN:v2p377/r4.anchor: قال الخوي واصلها لا وما لان النفي اما في الماضي واما في المستقبل

BURHAN:v2p419/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p419/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p419/r1.claim: The two emphatic nūns reinforce the verb, corresponding to the emphatic nominal particles إن and لام; the Qur'an uses the light emphatic nūn in only two places.
BURHAN:v2p419/r1.anchor: قيل وهذان النونان لتأكيد الفعل في مقابلة تأكيد الاسم بان واللام ولم يقع في القرآن التأكيد بالخفيفة

ITQAN:v3p157/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p157/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p157/r1.claim: One condition for ellipsis is evidence, which may come from the situation or wording; reason can also show that speech requires an omitted element.
ITQAN:v3p157/r1.anchor: أحدها وجود دليل إما حالي نحو ﴿ قالوا سلاما ﴾ أي سلمنا سلاما أو مقالي نحو ﴿ وقيل للذين اتقوا ماذا أنزل ربكم قالوا خيرا ﴾

ITQAN:v3p157/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p157/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p157/r7.claim: Custom selects the omitted phrase in the women’s reproach: although intellect shows that Joseph cannot literally be the place of blame, people do not ordinarily blame someone for involuntary excessive love, unlike seduction.
ITQAN:v3p157/r7.anchor: والعادة دلت على الثاني لأن الحب المفرط لا يلام صاحبه عليه عادة لأنه ليس اختياريا بخلاف المراودة للقدرة على دفعها

ITQAN:v2p520/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p520/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p520/r1.claim: The emphatic nūn is light or heavy; the light form occurs in only two Qurʾānic positions, including the seizure by the forelock, while 12:32 has the heavy form.
ITQAN:v2p520/r1.anchor: حرف وهي نوعان نون التوكيد وهي خفيفة وثقيلة نحو ﴿ ليسجنن وليكونن ﴾ ﴿ لنسفعا بالناصية ﴾ ولم تقع الخفيفة في القرآن إلا في هذين الموضعين

ITQAN:v3p207/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p207/r3.speaker: الخويي
ITQAN:v3p207/r3.claim: Al-Khūʾī says lā and mā are the original negative particles: lā is lighter than mā, so the lighter form was assigned to the more frequent future negation.
ITQAN:v3p207/r3.anchor: قال الخويي أصل أدوات النفي لا وما لأن النفي إما في الماضي وإما في المستقبل والاستقبال أكثر من الماضي أبدا

ITQAN:v3p207/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p207/r4.speaker: الخويي
ITQAN:v3p207/r4.claim: Al-Khūʾī derives four basic particles—mā, lam, lan, and lā—from past and future negation with different continuity patterns; in lam, lām points to lā and mīm to mā.
ITQAN:v3p207/r4.anchor: فصار النفي على أربعة أقسام واختاروا له أربع كلمات ما ولم ولن ولا وأما إن ولما فليسا بأصلين

ITQAN:v3p207/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p207/r5.speaker: الخويي
ITQAN:v3p207/r5.claim: He explains that lam combines the future-form lā with past mīm, while its lām precedes mīm because lā is the basis of negation and can join another negative in mid-sentence.
ITQAN:v3p207/r5.anchor: فأخذ اللام من ( لا ) التي هي لنفي المستقبل والميم من ( ما ) التي هي لنفي الماضي وجمع بينهما إشارة إلى أن في ( لم ) إشارة إلى المستقبل والماضي

ITQAN:v3p207/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p207/r6.speaker: الخويي
ITQAN:v3p207/r6.claim: He treats lammā as a layered lam plus mā that emphasizes past negation, also projects it into the future, and therefore conveys continuation: not yet.
ITQAN:v3p207/r6.anchor: وأما ( لما ) فتركيب بعد تركيب كأنه قال لم وما لتوكيد معنى النفي في الماضي وتفيد الاستقبال أيضا ولهذا تفيد ( لما ) الاستمرار

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p123/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p123/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p123/r1.claim: Meanings reached only through thought and toil invite greater esteem; even an easily found treasure recalls the labor of whoever earned or inherited it.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p123/r1.anchor: معلوم أن الشيء إذا علم أنه لم ينل في أصله إلا بعد التعب ولم يدرك إلا باحتمال النصب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p123/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p123/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p123/r2.claim: Al-Buhturi excels at making subtle, distant meanings familiar and easy to grasp, but not all his poetry is effortless or free of depth.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p123/r2.anchor: ما يعطى البحتري ويبلغ في هذا مبلغه فإنه ليروض لك المهر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p123/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p123/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p123/r3.claim: Al-Mutawakkil lost interest in the fine odes because he did not understand their meanings, unlike simpler poetry whose meanings he understood.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p123/r3.anchor: إلا لأنه لم يفهم معانيها كما فهم معاني النوع النازل الذي انحط له إليه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p123/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p123/r4.speaker: author
